# A bad dependency entry hides the other problems in the same group

## What happens now
When a group of extra dependencies in a project file holds an entry that is not a valid dependency, reading that group stops at that entry. The user sees only that one complaint. Any other problems found in the same group before it are thrown away, and the user never sees the message that says the group data was malformed.

## What should happen
When a group holds an entry that is not a valid dependency, the user should get one report that says the group data was malformed and lists every problem found in that group, including the bad entry and any others found at the same time.

## About this project
This project is a library that other Python tools use to read and understand project files. It reads the declared dependencies, the version ranges, and the named groups of extra dependencies that a project may define. Its job is to hand back a clean list of what to install, or a clear message when the project file does not make sense.

## Problem this solves
When one bad entry hides the other problems, the user has to fix one mistake, run the tool again, and repeat until the file is clean. Seeing all the problems for a group in one report lets them fix everything in a single pass.

## What changed
An entry that is not a valid dependency is now reported together with the other problems found in the same group, instead of stopping the report on its own. The message that names the group as malformed is now shown for this case too. Nothing else about reading a group behaves differently.

## Impact
Clearer error messages, ease of use, and fewer repeated runs to clean up a project file.

## User experience
Before: a user has a group with one empty item and one text entry that is not a valid dependency, and runs the tool on that group. They get only the complaint about the bad text entry, and the empty item problem is lost. They fix the text entry, run again, and only then see the empty item problem. After: the very same run gives one report that names the group as malformed and shows both problems together, so they can fix both at once.

## Hints
- /workspace/src/packaging/dependency_groups.py
- /workspace/src/packaging/errors.py
- /workspace/tests/test_dependency_groups.py
I'll start by reading the briefing, ticket, and hints files.

1 │ from __future__ import annotations
   2 │ 
   3 │ import re
   4 │ from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
   5 │ 
   6 │ from .errors import _ErrorCollector
   7 │ from .requirements import Requirement
   8 │ 
   9 │ __all__ = [
  10 │     "CyclicDependencyGroup",
  11 │     "DependencyGroupInclude",
  12 │     "DependencyGroupResolver",
  13 │     "DuplicateGroupNames",
  14 │     "InvalidDependencyGroupObject",
  15 │     "resolve_dependency_groups",
  16 │ ]
  17 │ 
  18 │ 
  19 │ def __dir__() -> list[str]:
  20 │     return __all__
  21 │ 
  22 │ 
  23 │ # -----------
  24 │ # Error Types
  25 │ # -----------
  26 │ 
  27 │ 
  28 │ class DuplicateGroupNames(ValueError):
  29 │     """
  30 │     The same dependency groups were defined twice, with different non-normalized names.
  31 │ 
  32 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  33 │     """
  34 │ 
  35 │ 
  36 │ class CyclicDependencyGroup(ValueError):
  37 │     """
  38 │     The dependency group includes form a cycle.
  39 │ 
  40 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  41 │     """
  42 │ 
  43 │     def __init__(self, requested_group: str, group: str, include_group: str) -> None:
  44 │         self.requested_group = requested_group
  45 │         self.group = group
  46 │         self.include_group = include_group
  47 │ 
  48 │         if include_group == group:
  49 │             reason = f"{group} includes itself"
  50 │         else:
  51 │             reason = f"{include_group} -> {group}, {group} -> {include_group}"
  52 │         super().__init__(
  53 │             "Cyclic dependency group include while resolving "
  54 │             f"{requested_group}: {reason}"
  55 │         )
  56 │ 
  57 │ 
  58 │ # in the PEP 735 spec, the tables in dependency group lists were described as
  59 │ # "Dependency Object Specifiers", but the only defined type of object was a
  60 │ # "Dependency Group Include" -- hence the naming of this error as "Object"
  61 │ class InvalidDependencyGroupObject(ValueError):
  62 │     """
  63 │     A member of a dependency group was identified as a dict, but was not in a valid
  64 │     format.
  65 │ 
  66 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  67 │     """
  68 │ 
  69 │ 
  70 │ # ------------------------
  71 │ # Object Model & Interface
  72 │ # ------------------------
  73 │ 
  74 │ 
  75 │ class DependencyGroupInclude:
  76 │     """
  77 │     A reference to another dependency group by name.
  78 │ 
  79 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
  80 │     """
  81 │ 
  82 │     __slots__ = ("include_group",)
  83 │ 
  84 │     def __init__(self, include_group: str) -> None:
  85 │         """
  86 │         Initialize a DependencyGroupInclude.
  87 │ 
  88 │         :param include_group: The name of the group referred to by this include.
  89 │         """
  90 │         self.include_group = include_group
  91 │ 
  92 │     def __repr__(self) -> str:
  93 │         return f"{self.__class__.__name__}({self.include_group!r})"
  94 │ 
  95 │ 
  96 │ class DependencyGroupResolver:
  97 │     """
  98 │     A resolver for Dependency Group data.
  99 │ 
 100 │     This class handles caching, name normalization, cycle detection, and other
 101 │     parsing requirements. There are only two public methods for exploring the data:
 102 │     ``lookup()`` and ``resolve()``.
 103 │ 
 104 │     :param dependency_groups: A mapping, as provided via pyproject
 105 │         ``[dependency-groups]``.
 106 │ 
 107 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 108 │     """
 109 │ 
 110 │     def __init__(
 111 │         self,
 112 │         dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]],
 113 │     ) -> None:
 114 │         errors = _ErrorCollector()
 115 │ 
 116 │         self.dependency_groups = _normalize_group_names(dependency_groups, errors)
 117 │ 
 118 │         # a map of group names to parsed data
 119 │         self._parsed_groups: dict[
 120 │             str, tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]
 121 │         ] = {}
 122 │         # a map of group names to their ancestors, used for cycle detection
 123 │         self._include_graph_ancestors: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
 124 │         # a cache of completed resolutions to Requirement lists
 125 │         self._resolve_cache: dict[str, tuple[Requirement, ...]] = {}
 126 │ 
 127 │         errors.finalize("[dependency-groups] data was invalid")
 128 │ 
 129 │     def lookup(self, group: str) -> tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]:
 130 │         """
 131 │         Lookup a group name, returning the parsed dependency data for that group.
 132 │         This will not resolve includes.
 133 │ 
 134 │         :param group: the name of the group to lookup
 135 │         """
 136 │         group = _normalize_name(group)
 137 │ 
 138 │         with _ErrorCollector().on_exit(
 139 │             f"[dependency-groups] data for {group!r} was malformed"
 140 │         ) as errors:
 141 │             return self._parse_group(group, errors)
 142 │ 
 143 │     def resolve(self, group: str) -> tuple[Requirement, ...]:
 144 │         """
 145 │         Resolve a dependency group to a list of requirements.
 146 │ 
 147 │         :param group: the name of the group to resolve
 148 │         """
 149 │         group = _normalize_name(group)
 150 │ 
 151 │         with _ErrorCollector().on_exit(
 152 │             f"[dependency-groups] data for {group!r} was malformed"
 153 │         ) as errors:
 154 │             return self._resolve(group, group, errors)
 155 │ 
 156 │     def _resolve(
 157 │         self, group: str, requested_group: str, errors: _ErrorCollector
 158 │     ) -> tuple[Requirement, ...]:
 159 │         """
 160 │         This is a helper for cached resolution to strings. It preserves the name of the
 161 │         group which the user initially requested in order to present a clearer error in
 162 │         the event that a cycle is detected.
 163 │ 
 164 │         :param group: The normalized name of the group to resolve.
 165 │         :param requested_group: The group which was used in the original, user-facing
 166 │             request.
 167 │         """
 168 │         if group in self._resolve_cache:
 169 │             return self._resolve_cache[group]
 170 │ 
 171 │         parsed = self._parse_group(group, errors)
 172 │ 
 173 │         resolved_group = []
 174 │ 
 175 │         for item in parsed:
 176 │             if isinstance(item, Requirement):
 177 │                 resolved_group.append(item)
 178 │             elif isinstance(item, DependencyGroupInclude):
 179 │                 include_group = _normalize_name(item.include_group)
 180 │ 
 181 │                 # if a group is cyclic, record the error
 182 │                 # otherwise, follow the include_group reference
 183 │                 #
 184 │                 # this allows us to examine all includes in a group, even in the
 185 │                 # presence of errors
 186 │                 if include_group in self._include_graph_ancestors.get(group, ()):
 187 │                     errors.error(
 188 │                         CyclicDependencyGroup(
 189 │                             requested_group, group, item.include_group
 190 │                         )
 191 │                     )
 192 │                 else:
 193 │                     self._include_graph_ancestors[include_group] = (
 194 │                         *self._include_graph_ancestors.get(group, ()),
 195 │                         group,
 196 │                     )
 197 │                     resolved_group.extend(
 198 │                         self._resolve(include_group, requested_group, errors)
 199 │                     )
 200 │             else:  # pragma: no cover
 201 │                 raise NotImplementedError(
 202 │                     f"Invalid dependency group item after parse: {item}"
 203 │                 )
 204 │ 
 205 │         # in the event that errors were detected, present the group as empty and do not
 206 │         # cache the result
 207 │         # this ensures that repeated access to a cyclic group will raise multiple errors
 208 │         if errors.errors:
 209 │             return ()
 210 │ 
 211 │         self._resolve_cache[group] = tuple(resolved_group)
 212 │         return self._resolve_cache[group]
 213 │ 
 214 │     def _parse_group(
 215 │         self, group: str, errors: _ErrorCollector
 216 │     ) -> tuple[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude, ...]:
 217 │         # short circuit -- never do the work twice
 218 │         if group in self._parsed_groups:
 219 │             return self._parsed_groups[group]
 220 │ 
 221 │         if group not in self.dependency_groups:
 222 │             errors.error(LookupError(f"Dependency group '{group}' not found"))
 223 │             return ()
 224 │ 
 225 │         raw_group = self.dependency_groups[group]
 226 │         if isinstance(raw_group, str):
 227 │             errors.error(
 228 │                 TypeError(
 229 │                     f"Dependency group {group!r} contained a string rather than a list."
 230 │                 )
 231 │             )
 232 │             return ()
 233 │ 
 234 │         if not isinstance(raw_group, Sequence):
 235 │             errors.error(
 236 │                 TypeError(f"Dependency group {group!r} is not a sequence type.")
 237 │             )
 238 │             return ()
 239 │ 
 240 │         elements: list[Requirement | DependencyGroupInclude] = []
 241 │         for item in raw_group:
 242 │             if isinstance(item, str):
 243 │                 # packaging.requirements.Requirement parsing ensures that this is a
 244 │                 # valid PEP 508 Dependency Specifier
 245 │                 # raises InvalidRequirement on failure
 246 │                 elements.append(Requirement(item))
 247 │             elif isinstance(item, Mapping):
 248 │                 if tuple(item.keys()) != ("include-group",):
 249 │                     errors.error(
 250 │                         InvalidDependencyGroupObject(
 251 │                             f"Invalid dependency group item: {item!r}"
 252 │                         )
 253 │                     )
 254 │                 else:
 255 │                     include_group = item["include-group"]
 256 │                     if not isinstance(include_group, str):
 257 │                         msg = (
 258 │                             "Dependency group include-group value is not a string: "
 259 │                             f"{item!r}"
 260 │                         )
 261 │                         errors.error(TypeError(msg))
 262 │                     else:
 263 │                         elements.append(
 264 │                             DependencyGroupInclude(include_group=include_group)
 265 │                         )
 266 │             else:
 267 │                 errors.error(TypeError(f"Invalid dependency group item: {item!r}"))
 268 │ 
 269 │         if errors.errors:
 270 │             return ()
 271 │ 
 272 │         self._parsed_groups[group] = tuple(elements)
 273 │         return self._parsed_groups[group]
 274 │ 
 275 │ 
 276 │ # --------------------
 277 │ # Functional Interface
 278 │ # --------------------
 279 │ 
 280 │ 
 281 │ def resolve_dependency_groups(
 282 │     dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]], /, *groups: str
 283 │ ) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 284 │     """
 285 │     Resolve a dependency group to a tuple of requirements, as strings.
 286 │ 
 287 │     :param dependency_groups: the parsed contents of the ``[dependency-groups]`` table
 288 │         from ``pyproject.toml``
 289 │     :param groups: the name of the group(s) to resolve
 290 │ 
 291 │     .. versionadded:: 26.1
 292 │     """
 293 │     resolver = DependencyGroupResolver(dependency_groups)
 294 │     return tuple(str(r) for group in groups for r in resolver.resolve(group))
 295 │ 
 296 │ 
 297 │ # ----------------
 298 │ # internal helpers
 299 │ # ----------------
 300 │ 
 301 │ 
 302 │ _NORMALIZE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[-_.]+")
 303 │ 
 304 │ 
 305 │ def _normalize_name(name: str) -> str:
 306 │     return _NORMALIZE_PATTERN.sub("-", name).lower()
 307 │ 
 308 │ 
 309 │ def _normalize_group_names(
 310 │     dependency_groups: Mapping[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]],
 311 │     errors: _ErrorCollector,
 312 │ ) -> dict[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]]:
 313 │     original_names: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
 314 │     normalized_groups: dict[str, Sequence[str | Mapping[str, str]]] = {}
 315 │ 
 316 │     for group_name, value in dependency_groups.items():
 317 │         normed_group_name = _normalize_name(group_name)
 318 │         original_names.setdefault(normed_group_name, []).append(group_name)
 319 │         normalized_groups[normed_group_name] = value
 320 │ 
 321 │     for normed_name, names in original_names.items():
 322 │         if len(names) > 1:
 323 │             errors.error(
 324 │                 DuplicateGroupNames(
 325 │                     "Duplicate dependency group names: "
 326 │                     f"{normed_name} ({', '.join(names)})"
 327 │                 )
 328 │             )
 329 │ 
 330 │     return normalized_groups
 331 │
